answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making influence cost locked capital plus time. To gain voting weight, an agent escrows tokens for a fixed period, and weight grows with the square root of the stake, so splitting into many identities yields less than one large stake. Stakes are slashed if an identity is caught colluding. Like a lotus rooting in mud, reputation must grow slowly from the nadir, so a fresh account starts at zero weight. An attacker forging a hundred onyx-grade identities must lock a hundred stakes for months, then risk losing them all.
